decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Quarter 2 2025/26 Budget Monitoring Report
will set out the Council’s latest forecast year end position
for revenue and capital expenditure and income, including
management actions being taken, financial performance information
including income collection, debt recovery, treasury management and
reserves. The report will contain decisions relating to capital and
revenue expenditure, savings and income that will address the
council’s financial position both in year and for future
years.
content:
The item was introduced by Councillor Judith
Cavanagh, Cabinet Member for Finance (Acting). The following key
points were highlighted:
•        
The Q2 report provided an expanded update on performance,
transparency and oversight, with forecast overspends driven by
accommodation costs, adult and children’s social care, and
debt financing.
•        
The Council had implemented strict spending controls including a
20% reduction in senior management, a freeze on non-essential
recruitment, reductions in agency staff and a pause on
non-essential capital borrowing.
•        
More than 80% of 2025/26 savings were delivered or on track, and
£28m in early savings proposals were brought forward to
support the 2026/27 budget.

Councillor Martin Abrams, visiting Member,
addressed the meeting and raised the following points:
•        
The report showed significant financial strain and raised concerns
about the lack of a clear strategy to stabilise temporary
accommodation and social care budgets.
•        
Concerns were raised about the reliance on savings not yet
identified for 2026/27, including over £35 million of future
savings, and the risk of deferring difficult decisions.
•        
The Council was urged to strengthen transparency and planning by
fully scrutinising auditor recommendations, being clearer with
residents about what was deliverable, revisiting the Borough Plan
to reflect available resources, and intensifying public lobbying of
central government for a fair funding deal.
Marietta Crichton Stuart, Friends of
Kennington Park, addressed the meeting and highlighted:
•        
Concern about the pause of funding for the Kennington Park Skate
Bowl despite six years of preparatory work.
•        
The value of the skate bowl in supporting young people’s
wellbeing, community cohesion and local heritage.
•        
The potential increased cost and risk associated with mothballing
or removing the bowl if restoration did not proceed.
Sophy Tayler, SE5 Forum / Lambeth Forum
Network, addressed the meeting and highlighted:
•        
Concern about the proposed £60,000 reduction to forum funding
and the limited notice provided to voluntary groups.
•        
The importance of core funding in enabling forums to attract
external grants, noting £1.2 million leveraged in the
previous year.
•        
The negative impact the cut could have on community projects
relating to health, safety, climate and neighbourhood
engagement.
In response to comments, Councillor Claire
Holland, Leader of the Council, stated that the Council was taking
difficult decisions immediately rather than deferring action. The
role of scrutiny committees and the Corporate Committee in
reviewing the Council’s finances was highlighted.
Officers advised the following:
•        
Savings proposals for future years would be brought forward through
the Medium-Term Financial Strategy in January.
•        
The Skate Bowl was part of a wider capital review to reduce
borrowing, with decisions on paused projects due shortly and
prioritisation necessary due to high interest costs.
•        
Early notification of the Forum Network saving was deliberate to
allow time to work with forums on potential mitigations.
•        
Officers advised that they were working with organisations to
identify wider support, including help to seek alternative funding,
alongside continued officer assistance.
•        
Proposed changes would not take effect until the next financial
year, allowing time to continue this work.
•        
The Council would continue working with Transport for London, the
Greater London Authority (GLA) and other London bodies to lobby for
greater local powers and devolution, including the ability to use
enforcement measures such as cameras in response to
residents’ priorities.
In response to questions and comments, Cabinet
Members noted the following:
•        
Temporary accommodation remained the biggest financial pressure,
and reducing reliance on costly nightly paid placements was central
to the Council’s strategy.
•        
Renegotiation of contracts and improved procurement had delivered
over £1.3 million in savings this year, with further savings
projected.
•        
A new placement policy would build on work to help more families
move into the private rented sector, improving stability and
reducing costs.
•        
It was noted that the adaptive street lighting project had been
paused pending the financial review, and clarification was provided
that the scheme was not progressing at this stage due to current
budget considerations.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to implement strict spending controls and bring forward savings proposals to address financial strain and budget cuts in various areas.

decision_maker: Assistant Director - Parking, Network Management and Fleet
content:
1.            
To have due regard to the engagement activity undertaken through
two stages (October 2024 to January 2025 and April to May 2025)
with local residents, stakeholders, and statutory consultees during
the development of the Voltaire Road Reimagined proposals, as
detailed in Section 5 of this report and summarised
in Appendix A and Appendix B – Concerns Raised and
Officer Response Table.
 
2.            
To have due regard to the Equality Impact Assessment attached at
Appendix C.
 
3.            
To authorise officers to carry out a statutory consultation under
Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure)
(England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996 Regulations), prior
to the implementation of the Voltaire Road reimagined scheme
detailed in this report, under an Experimental Traffic Management
Order (“Experimental TMO”) made under the provisions of
Sections 9 and 10 of the Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 and
Regulation 22 of the Local Authorities’ Traffic Orders
(Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996. The proposed
scheme is outlined in Appendix D.
 
4.            
To delegate authority to the Assistant Director – Parking,
Network Management and Fleet, having due regard to the outcome of
statutory consultation under Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities
Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996
(the 1996 Regulations), to authorise any modifications to the
Experimental TMO that are considered necessary as a result of any
objections being received or incapable of satisfactory resolution
by modifications to the Experimental TMO.
 
5.            
That, subject to the outcome of the statutory consultation under
Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure)
(England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996 Regulations), to
authorise the implementation of the scheme detailed in this report,
under an Experimental Traffic Management Order (“Experimental
TMO”) made under the provisions of Sections 9 and 10 of the
Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 and Regulation 22 of the Local
Authorities’ Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996.
 
6.            
That, subject to the outcome of the statutory consultation under
Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure)
(England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996 Regulations) and
scheme approval being given, that after consultation with the Chief
Officer of Police, any modifications to the Experimental TMO which
renders it less restrictive may be authorised by the Assistant
Director, Parking, Network Management and Fleet, without the
requirement to re-advertise the Order under Section 10(2) of the
said Act.
 
7.            
That, subject to the outcome of the statutory consultation under
Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities Traffic Orders (Procedure)
(England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996 Regulations) and
scheme approval being given, that any valid objections received
within the six month period under Schedule 5 of the Local
Authorities’ Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996 be considered by way of a written report to the
Assistant Director, Parking, Network Management and Fleet before a
decision is reached on whether or not any of the provisions of the
experimental order will be made permanent.
 
8.            
To undertake a non-statutory consultation exercise with local
stakeholders prior to any decision being made on moving to a
permanent traffic order.
 
9.            
To approve the projected spend of £67,647 by the end of
2025.

decision_maker: Deputy Leader of the Council (Sustainable Lambeth and Clean Air)
purpose:
Approval to implement a trial healthy
neighbourhood scheme, known as Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens, under an
experimental traffic order. Trial experimental traffic restrictions
are proposed for the area bounded by Albert Embankment (A3032),
Kennington Lane (A3204) and Black Prince Road to reduce road danger
and enable safe walking, wheeling, scooting and cycling.

The scheme is a combination of traffic restrictions and public
realm improvements with kerbside initiatives to significantly
improve walking, wheeling, scooting and cycling to create
healthier, greener and safer streets while retaining access for
motor vehicles.
content:
1.            
To have due regard to the engagement activity undertaken through
two stages with local residents, stakeholders, and statutory
consultees during the development of the Vauxhall Pleasure Gardens
Healthy Neighbourhood proposals, as detailed in Section 5 of this
report and summarised in Appendix A and Appendix B –
Concerns Raised and Officer Response Table.
2.            
To note the Equality Impact Assessment attached at Appendix C.
3.            
To note scheme approval provided by the Phase 3 Transport Programme
– Capital Drawdown report of 10/09/2024 for Vauxhall Pleasure
Gardens Healthy Neighbourhood trial in the area bounded by Albert
Embankment (A3032), Kennington Lane (A3204) and Black Prince Road
as illustrated in Appendix D, under Section 2.
4.            
That, having given due regard to the outcome of the engagement
activity with local residents and stakeholders and the statutory
consultation under Regulation 6 of the Local Authorities Traffic
Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996 (the 1996
Regulations), to implement the scheme detailed in this report,
under an Experimental Traffic Management Order (“Experimental
TMO”) made under the provisions of Sections 9 and 10 of the
Road Traffic Regulation Act 1984 and Regulation 22 of the Local
Authorities’ Traffic Orders (Procedure) (England and Wales)
Regulations 1996.
5.            
Following the outcome of the statutory consultation under
Regulation 6, to exercise discretion to not hold a public inquiry
pursuant to Regulation 9 of the Local Authorities Traffic Orders
(Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996.
6.            
That, after consultation with the Chief Officer of Police,
modifications to the Experimental Order which renders it less
restrictive may be authorised by the Assistant Director –
Parking, Network Management and Fleet, without the requirement to
re-advertise the Order under Section 10(2) of the said Act.
7.            
To undertake a non-statutory consultation exercise with local
stakeholders prior to any decision being made upon whether to make
the provisions of the experimental order permanent.
8.            
That any valid objections received within the six month period
under Schedule 5 of the Local Authorities’ Traffic Orders
(Procedure) (England and Wales) Regulations 1996 be considered by
way of a separate written report to the Deputy Leader of the
Council (Sustainable Lambeth and Clean Air) before a decision is
reached on whether any of the provisions of the experimental order
will be made permanent and on whether a public inquiry should be
held in relation to the permanent order.
9.            
To approve the projected spend of £188,100 by the end of
2025, externally funded through S106 developer contributions

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
Lambeth’s Night Time Strategy will set
out the council’s vision for becoming more welcoming,
accessible, safe and equitable between 6 pm and 6 am.

The strategy will also seek to address the cost of living and
trading crises by supporting night time economy businesses and
cultural venues. It will also align with work to increase the
number of Living Wage Accredited employers in the borough and
improve working conditions for night time workers.
content:
Councillor Marcia Cameron also introduced the
item and highlighted the following key points:
 

The strategy was a key component of
the Lambeth Growth Plan which aimed to celebrate Lambeth’s
24-hour identity, supporting inclusive economic growth, community
engagement, and safety.


It sought to protect and enhance the
borough’s cultural and creative offer while ensuring a safe
and welcoming environment for residents and visitors.
The strategy was developed through a
ground-up approach informed by lessons from the Vauxhall Night-Time
Enterprise Zone pilot.

 
Following introduction, Cabinet Members raised
the following points:
 

The importance of community safety
and safeguarding, particularly for younger residents using the
night-time economy was highlighted.
It was suggested that schools, youth
services, and safeguarding partners should be closely involved in
delivery.
The inclusion of all town centres in
the strategy and the opportunity to support local neighbourhoods
with extended opening hours was welcomed.
It was noted that new national and
regional powers could be used to support local businesses and
revive high streets.

Officers then provided the following responses
to questions:

Officers confirmed that consultation
sessions had been held with both older and younger residents,
ensuring diverse perspectives were captured.
They explained that young people had
identified cost and safety as key issues, and that the strategy
included actions to address these through targeted events and
partnerships.
Officers advised that delivery would
align with the Council’s Child Friendly Lambeth commitments
and the Safer Lambeth Partnership.
It was confirmed that collaboration
across departments and agencies would ensure a coordinated and
inclusive approach to implementation.
Lambeth was well positioned to
contribute to forthcoming London-wide discussions on licensing
reform, including proposals for economic growth as a licensing
objective, and to provide evidence-based feedback to future policy
consultations due to participation in The Summer Streets
initiative.

 
RESOLVED:

1.   
To approve and adopt the Lambeth Night
Time Economy Strategy for delivery between 2025-2030.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve and adopt the Lambeth Night Time Economy Strategy for delivery between 2025-2030.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The decision for Cabinet is to approve the
Inclusive Talent Strategy 2025 – 2030, which is a refresh of
the previous Skills and Employment Strategy. This strategy provides
the overarching framework and key ambitions for what the Council
hopes its activity in skills and employment will achieve over the
next five years.
content:
The item was introduced by Councillor Marcia
Cameron, Cabinet Member for Economic Inclusion. The following key
points were highlighted:
 

The Strategy formed part of the
Lambeth Growth Plan and contributed to achieving Lambeth’s
2030 Borough Plan ambition of equity and justice for all.
It aimed to create skills and
employment opportunities for all communities, improving financial
stability and prosperity for residents, particularly young people,
economically inactive individuals, and those with
disabilities.
The strategy was supported by a
detailed action plan with measurable ambitions and
partnership-based delivery.

 
In response to questions raised by Members,
officers advised the following:
 

The strategy was informed by
consultation with residents, partners, and community
organisations.
It was confirmed that priority
groups, such as lone parents and residents furthest from
employment, were identified using local data and feedback.
Officers explained that the strategy
adopted a trauma-informed and flexible approach, allowing delivery
to adapt to changing economic conditions.
They noted that the framework would
encourage cross-council collaboration and alignment with regional
strategies.

 
Cabinet Members provided the following
feedback to the strategy:
 

Members commended the focus on
supporting local priority groups and ensuring that opportunities
were tailored to residents’ needs.
The strategy was described as a key
tool in tackling structural inequalities and embedding fairness
within Lambeth’s economic growth agenda.

 
RESOLVED:

1.   
To approve and adopt the Lambeth Inclusive Talent Strategy, taking
effect from October 2025, as our strategic direction for skills and
employment activity across the borough.
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve and adopt the Lambeth Inclusive Talent Strategy to create skills and employment opportunities for all communities in the borough.

decision_maker: Cabinet
purpose:
The Creative Industries are a priority growth
area for the borough and national government. This inclusive growth
strategy will lay out the council’s commitments to strengthen
Lambeth’s cultural and creative ecosystem, so it can thrive
in ways that enable all residents to contribute to, and benefit
from, a vibrant and dynamic creative economy.
content:
Councillor Marcia Cameron also introduced the
item and noted that:
 

This was the third enabling strategy
within the Lambeth Growth Plan alongside the Inclusive Talent and
Night-Time Economy strategies, aimed to position Lambeth as a
leading creative borough by promoting growth, sustainability, and
inclusivity across the creative and cultural sectors.
It sought to nurture creative
talent, support businesses, and increase access to career pathways
for underrepresented groups.
The strategy provided a framework
linking creative industries with education, skills, regeneration,
and economic development initiatives.

 
In response to questions, officers advised
that:
 

The strategy aimed to help grassroot
cultural organisations access new technologies and build digital
and AI skills through partnerships, enabling them to innovate and
benefit from emerging creative opportunities.
Programmes like Next Us, funded by the Mayor of
London, sought to break down barriers for vulnerable young people,
including those not in education, employment or training and
care-experienced residents, helping them pursue creative
careers.
The Council continued to invest in
cultural spaces across the borough, including projects in West
Norwood and Streatham, using grant funding to support smaller
organisations and attract new cultural operators through
community-led engagement.
The Council worked through the
Lambeth Strategic Partnership and Skills and Employment Board to
align major cultural institutions with borough priorities,
strengthening links between culture, education, and
employment.
The strategy was developed with
input from a representative group including organisations of
varying size and freelancers, ensuring actions were tested across
the sector.
Borough-wide equity was also
embedded into programmes to ensure that investment and grant
funding opportunities were distributed fairly across all
areas.

 
RESOLVED:

1.   
To approve and adopt the Lambeth’s Creative Economy Strategy
in October 2025
topline: The Cabinet has decided to approve and adopt Lambeth's Creative Economy Strategy in October 2025.

decision_maker: Director of Economy, Skills, and Culture
purpose:
This report seeks approval to award a contract
to Unboxed Consulting Ltd (hereafter titled ‘Unboxed’)
for the provision of the Research and Development (R and D –
to include User Research and other disciplines) input into the
Building Control Alpha project. The provision will be funded by the
Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government (MHCLG)
digital strategic projects grant funding, which is ringfenced and
has been awarded to Lambeth Council specifically for the engagement
of specialists necessary to deliver the project. The provision of
this work is therefore cost neutral to the Council.

The proposed contract has been procured via G-Cloud 14, where a
direct award was undertaken after entering required search
criteria. The criteria used for this search on G Cloud 14, was
“Prototype”, “End to end” and
“Stakeholder Mapping”. This resulted in three suppliers
being identified and these were Marvell Consulting Ltd, Unboxed and
Ove Arup and Partners Ltd. This resulted in confirmation questions
being sent to all suppliers and based on the review of the
information available, the contract is to be awarded to
Unboxed.
content:
To approve the award of a contract
to Unboxed Consulting Ltd for the provision of Research and
Development (R and D – to include User Research and other
disciplines) input into the Building Control Alpha project funded
through MHCLG grant funding via a Direct Award through the Crown
Commercial Services (CCS) G-Cloud 14 for the period starting in
October 2025 for six months at a cost of £185,000.
topline: The Director of Economy, Skills, and Culture has decided to award a contract to Unboxed Consulting Ltd for Research and Development input into the Building Control Alpha project.
